key_insight: A systematic, empirical quantification shows that both individual modules and their interactions in the PSO-X modular PSO framework substantially influence optimization performance — interaction effects can be as important as single-module effects.
problem_solved: Addresses the complexity of choosing and configuring dozens of interchangeable modules in the PSO-X framework by measuring which modules and module combinations actually drive performance, so practitioners can prioritize components and reduce configuration search space.
method: Large-scale, controlled experiments across benchmark continuous optimization problems to measure performance changes when enabling/disabling modules.
Statistical decomposition of performance variance to quantify main effects (individual modules) and interaction effects (module pairs/groups), producing ranked importance measures.
Aggregated analysis to identify robustly beneficial modules and problematic interactions, yielding practical guidance for algorithm configuration and automated design.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners and AutoML systems focus on high-impact modules and avoid costly combinatorial tuning; improves efficiency and reliability when building or auto-configuring PSO-based optimizers.
visual_elements: Bar chart of module effect sizes (main effects) sorted by importance
Heatmap or network diagram showing pairwise interaction strengths among modules
Pipeline schematic of the PSO-X modular architecture with icons for module categories (initialization, velocity, update rules, etc.)
Flowchart summarizing the evaluation protocol (benchmarks → factorial sampling → variance decomposition → recommendations)
paper_title: Quantifying the Impact of Modules and Their Interactions in the PSO-X Framework
paper_authors: Christian L. Camacho-Villalón, Ana Nikolikj, Katharina Dost, Eva Tuba, Sašo Džeroski
